flags: Corteva completed the separation of its seed operating segment into an independent public company, Vylor Inc., by pro rata distribution to Corteva shareholders.
Management approved the 2026 Restructuring Actions, mainly workforce reductions, ahead of the separation. The company reports they are expected to be substantially complete by December 2026.

news.headline: Corteva investirá US$ 3,2 milhões em unidade de SP para formular novo fungicida
news.quote: Corteva investe US$ 3,2 milhões em unidade de SP para formular fungicida para soja

touches.claim: Post-spin Corteva's crop-protection market weakened in Brazil. Pro forma Q3 net sales fell (9)%, with Latin America down (28)% and price down (7)%, and full-year guidance was updated for weaker Brazil conditions.

Strength is concentrated in differentiated new products and in regions outside Latin America. Pro forma third-quarter net sales changed (28)% in Latin America, against 7% in North America and 12% in EMEA.

Brazil crop protection is the main named competitive and market threat. Management cites farmer liquidity constraints, elevated financing costs, just-in-time purchasing and pricing pressure, and updated full-year guidance as a result. Adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA is now guided to $1.1 to $1.125 billion.

New Crop Protection products are the volume offset to the weak Brazil market. For this to continue, demand for new products must hold and regional performance outside Latin America must stay resilient.

Recovery of the Brazil Crop Protection market is the key condition. Management cut its full-year outlook because Brazil was weaker than expected, and Latin America net sales fell (28)% in the third quarter.

business_model.claim: Corteva sells agricultural inputs, seed and crop protection products, to farmers worldwide. Through the 2025 10-K it was managed as two operating segments, Seed and Crop Protection.
quotes: The company’s operations are managed through two operating segments: Seed and Crop Protection.
The Crop Protection segment supplies products to protect crop yields against weeds, insects and disease, enabling farmers to achieve optimal results.

business_model.claim: The Seed segment was separated into a standalone company, Vylor Inc., on October 1, 2026, the day after the quarter ended. The company now describes itself as a global crop protection company, so the go-forward business is mainly Crop Protection.

is a global crop protection company with a leading portfolio of differentiated solutions

business_model.claim: By geography, pro forma third-quarter 2026 net sales (table in millions) were North America 574, EMEA 239, Latin America 570 and Asia Pacific 208, for a total of 1,591. Latin America is about as large as North America in this period.

Sales are seasonal. About 60 percent of sales came in the first half of the calendar year (driven by northern hemisphere Seed and Crop Protection) and about 40 percent in the second half. Receivables tend to be higher in the first half, with cash collection focused in the fourth quarter.
quotes: The company typically generates about 60 percent of its sales in the first half of the calendar year, driven by northern hemisphere Seed and Crop Protection sales.

quotes: reflecting a 6 percent decrease in volume and a 2 percent decrease in price, partially offset by a 2 percent favorable impact from currency.
